faqs.a: Mean is the average (sum ÷ count). Median is the middle value when sorted. Mean reacts strongly to outliers; median does not — so report the median for skewed data like incomes.
faqs.q: Mean vs median — which should I report?

faqs.a: The mode is the most frequent value. A dataset can have one mode, several modes (multimodal), or no mode at all when every value appears once. This calculator lists every mode it finds.
faqs.q: Can data have more than one mode?

faqs.a: Quartiles split sorted data into quarters: Q1 is the 25th percentile, Q3 the 75th. The IQR (Q3 − Q1) covers the middle 50% of values and is the standard robust measure of spread.
faqs.q: What are quartiles and the IQR?

faqs.a: The 1.5×IQR rule: values below Q1 − 1.5×IQR or above Q3 + 1.5×IQR are flagged as outliers. It is a rule of thumb, not a proof — always look at the data too.
faqs.q: How do I detect outliers with the IQR?

faqs.a: Use sample SD when your data is a subset standing in for a larger group; population SD when it is the entire group. For most real datasets, sample SD is the right choice.

statistics-calculator.formula:
Mean:    x̄ = Σx / n
Median:  middle value of sorted data (average of two middles if n is even)
Mode:    most frequent value(s)
Range:   max − min
Quartiles: Q1 = 25th percentile, Q3 = 75th percentile (linear interpolation)
IQR:     Q3 − Q1
Sample variance: s² = Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1)

keyFacts: Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset's center, spread and shape in a few numbers.
The median is robust to outliers; the mean is not.
The IQR (Q3 − Q1) captures the middle 50% of the data.
Variance and SD come in sample (÷ n−1) and population (÷ n) versions.
A dataset can have zero, one, or several modes.

statistics-calculator.workedExample:
Data: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5  (n = 5)
Sum = 15, Mean = 15 / 5 = 3
Median = 3 (middle value)
Mode: none — every value appears once
Min = 1, Max = 5, Range = 5 − 1 = 4
Q1 = 2 (25th percentile), Q3 = 4 (75th percentile), IQR = 2
Squared deviations from 3: 4, 1, 0, 1, 4 → sum = 10
Sample variance = 10 / 4 = 2.5, Sample SD = √2.5 ≈ 1.5811
Population variance = 10 / 5 = 2, Population SD = √2 ≈ 1.4142
